what_it_proves: A daemon killed -Force mid-turn leaves its shim and its agent alive; a replacement daemon adopts the orphan, drains its buffer, and the result produced while no daemon existed lands exactly once.
why_real_machinery: Only a real process kill produces an orphaned shim; the adoption is a live named-pipe connect to a process that outlived its parent, and the buffer is real bytes it held while nothing was listening.

what_it_proves: Only the child is killed: the shim exits by itself, and its pipe name and its shim-lane<N>.json go with it.
why_real_machinery: A process must actually die and another must actually notice. The pipe namespace and the record file are OS state, not values a function returns; the PROCESS is asserted gone before the namespace is read, because a pipe name blinks.

what_it_proves: No daemon ever returns: the shim ends its own lease and takes the agent with it.
why_real_machinery: The lease is wall-clock inside a live shim process. Nothing in-process can observe a process deciding to end itself and taking a child with it.

what_it_proves: stop-all --lanes reaches a shim over its own pipe (##shutdown) and the child TREE dies with it.
why_real_machinery: Killing a child tree rather than orphaning it is an OS fact about grandchildren. It asserts only that this workspace's shim was reached, never that stop-all is machine-wide.

what_it_proves: Liveness is asked of the OS: ps still counts a lane whose shim-lane<N>.json has been deleted.
why_real_machinery: The claim is that the answer came from the process table and not from a file, which is only visible once the file is gone and the process is not.

what_it_proves: The spawn-site environment reaches the agent two process hops away (daemon -> shim -> child).
why_real_machinery: Two real process starts, and the claim is precisely that nothing in between rewrote the environment block on its way down.

what_it_proves: A command that promises a reading summons nothing: no daemon process appears and the lane count does not move.
why_real_machinery: An absence-of-process claim, which no unit test can make. It is the cheapest integration test in the repo and it guards quota, which is the scarce resource. NOTE: issue #13 records that the no-summon list is still a hand-maintained literal in Client and that ten verbs summon while reading like questions; when #13 lands and the list becomes enforcement, this owner_check is re-pointed in #13's own commit.

what_it_proves: A real gate-hook subprocess fed real stdin bytes including a UTF-8 BOM reaches the daemon over the ctl pipe, REFUSES a shared-checkout write, and the refusal promotes the lane: a real worktree appears, the agent is killed and respawned inside it, its session resumed and its briefing rebuilt as a ticket lane's.
why_real_machinery: A PreToolUse hook is a separate executable reading stdin, and the fail-open the BOM caused was reachable only by piping real bytes into the real exe. The promotion then creates a real git worktree and restarts a real agent process in it.

what_it_proves: The undo removes the worktree directory and the branch ref, after the agent has let go of the cwd.
why_real_machinery: A real git ref and a real directory must disappear, and on Windows the prune cannot succeed while a live process holds the cwd - that race is what the check is for.

what_it_proves: A real git merge main plus merge --ff-only advances exactly one repository's main carrying the branch's work, prunes the worktree, deletes the branch and retires the agent standing in it; the other repository's ref does not move.
why_real_machinery: A ref that MOVED is a different fact from a ref REPORTED moved (D-5), and only a real repository can tell them apart. Two real repositories are what make exactly-one assertable, and on Windows the prune succeeding is itself the proof the agent was killed.

what_it_proves: The configured verify runs as a real child process in the worktree and its exit code gates the ref advance BEFORE it: a red verify leaves main where it was.
why_real_machinery: The ordering claim - verify before the advance, not after - is only observable when both the child process and the ref mutation are real. This is the only check separating verify-before from verify-after.

what_it_proves: The land consults SilentDrops over the branch's real merge history and refuses a merge that succeeded and lost work.
why_real_machinery: The input is a real git merge history that a scripted repository has to produce, and the refusal has to leave a real ref where it was.

what_it_proves: The land runs off the serial control pipe: the daemon still answers another command while a land's verify is running.
why_real_machinery: A concurrency claim about one NamedPipeServerStream instance handling commands inline. It needs a real second client call landing while a real slow handler runs; reasoning about which thread runs what is what kept the freeze invisible for months.

what_it_proves: A ticket turn ending with the worktree moved fires the per-turn hook at the SPAWN site, produces a completion record, and opens a land question row without waiting for a review.
why_real_machinery: The trigger is a real agent turn crossing the shim wire into the daemon, and the not-waiting half is what must hold on a machine with judgement switched off - an absence around a real turn.

what_it_proves: That record reaches a real manager; its send-back returns to the working lane as input on the typed-sentence path; a manager approve grants nothing and answers nothing; a named changed file is handed over off disk, once.
why_real_machinery: Two live agent lanes talking through one daemon. The negative half - that approve advanced no ref and closed no question - is an absence measured across a real round trip.

what_it_proves: The send-back bound is counted in the STORE, so three is still three after a real daemon restart mid-loop.
why_real_machinery: The whole claim is that the counter is not in daemon memory, and only a real restart can show that.

what_it_proves: A daemon started the way the operator runs it - autostart on, nothing pre-built by the test - creates the classifier itself, a typed sentence reaches THAT lane, and the lane opens in the project the classifier chose.
why_real_machinery: This is the routing-ladder incident's own check. A suite that stands up its own classifier and then looks one up proves nothing: the create-side role and the use-side role must be shown to match on the path the operator actually runs.

what_it_proves: A real daemon restart ADOPTS every live utility lane over its pipe - one per project - spawning none and retiring none.
why_real_machinery: Adoption is a live pipe connect to a process that outlived the daemon, and spawning none and retiring none are absences over real processes.

what_it_proves: A live predecessor whose pipe cannot be connected is never duplicated nor written off as gone, and one project's wedge does not block another project getting a brain.
why_real_machinery: The fixture is a genuinely wedged pipe - a client slot held open against a live server - which has no in-process equivalent, and the outcome is counted in real spawned processes.

what_it_proves: A registry mutation reaps the live processes it orphans: detaching a project stops its lanes and its brain shim, and forgetting a workspace stops its now-orphaned daemon.
why_real_machinery: Real OS processes have to exit. A store row saying reaped is exactly the thing this check exists to disbelieve.

what_it_proves: The sentence decided in CODE takes the INSTANT path: a LANE: prefix is delivered to that lane with no classifier consulted and nothing held.
why_real_machinery: Two absences around a real delivery - no model process was consulted and no question row was written - on a path whose whole requirement is that it stays instant. Added by the adversarial review: m2's routing half had no destination suite, and cutting this reddens nothing else. OWNER CORRECTED (W3): tier0_message_delivered asserts only that the text ARRIVED, which the focus fallback also achieves -- under a mutant that removed the instant path it stayed GREEN. tier0_prefix_routes asserts the RUNG (-> SKY (tier 0)) and is the check that fails when this wire is cut.

what_it_proves: With no classifier the fallback ANNOUNCES itself and writes routing_unrouted; it never degrades in silence.
why_real_machinery: The routing ladder was dead in production for two days and the only evidence was a status-line suffix nobody reads. The announcement has to be observed on a live daemon that genuinely has no classifier. Added by the adversarial review: a list that keeps the detector (E1) and drops the alarm keeps the wrong half.

what_it_proves: A real brain turn runs BEHIND the instant code path and its verdict - the rename - lands on the lane row afterwards, gating nothing.
why_real_machinery: The point is that a second agent's turn overlapped a delivery that did not wait for it: a race between two real processes, which is what after-the-fact means here.

what_it_proves: Genuine uncertainty HOLDS the sentence as a questions row that outlives a daemon restart; answering it spawns the lane in the chosen project and delivers the stored words verbatim.
why_real_machinery: A real restart is what proves the held sentence was on disk rather than in memory, and the answer puts a real agent process in a chosen project's working directory.

what_it_proves: The compressor pool starts real sessions, a turn-final crosses to one over a real shim pipe, and the rewrite lands back on the row as compressed.
why_real_machinery: The pool is real child sessions; the assertion is a round trip out to a separate process and back onto the row the text came from.

what_it_proves: Text typed in the box crosses the UI pipe to the daemon, which creates and routes a lane, delivers the sentence to a real agent running where the daemon put it, and the agent's own answer - its text, its tool calls, its out-of-band wire fields - comes back into the pane.
why_real_machinery: The longest path in the product and the operator's own: a live WPF window, a named pipe, a daemon, a shim and a child process. NOTE: today this check reads pane_events, so it proves UI to daemon only; the plan requires it be strengthened to assert the AGENT'S OWN echo carries the newline before it is the owner of this wire.

what_it_proves: Enter through the real PreviewKeyDown path submits and Shift+Enter does not, raised as a routed event on the real TextBox.
why_real_machinery: With AcceptsReturn on, WPF's TextBox class handler eats Enter before an instance KeyDown, so only a real routed event on a real control has the class handler in the way. NOTE: survey-window records that ui type and ui key call SubmitInput/InputKey directly rather than synthesizing a keystroke, so no check in the repo proves this today - this row is an UNCOVERED wire that the migration must build, not a duplicated one.

what_it_proves: A real WPF layout measures the multiline box: it opens at three lines, drags taller, and the FEED gives up the pixels so the window never moves.
why_real_machinery: MinLines and MaxLines are ignored once TextWrapping is on, so the default height is a MEASURED MinHeight. With no layout pass fit is 0 and this goes red specifically, where the sibling checks pass vacuously.

what_it_proves: A real UIA Invoke() on a rendered control reaches MainWindow.LaneAction and the daemon acts, across all five tile actions.
why_real_machinery: The five tile actions were unreachable rather than merely untested. The link from a rendered control to the daemon acting exists only through a real automation tree that has published a named element.

what_it_proves: Nothing lives in the window's memory: a relaunched window process restores collapse from the store, and box height plus listen toggle from ui.json.
why_real_machinery: A genuinely new process must read back what the old one wrote. A single process cannot make that claim about itself, and there are two stores of record (the store and a preference file) to read back.

what_it_proves: A real window renders deterministic pixels at a fixed size.
why_real_machinery: RenderTargetBitmap renders in the element's own coordinate space, so the capture has to be of a real Window rather than a margined child. Pixels are the only evidence a dump cannot fabricate.

what_it_proves: The mic affordance: a real UIA invoke and the listen verb both land in SetListening; a real socket to a closed loopback port reads as ERROR, not listening; and Starting has a deadline that fires.
why_real_machinery: A socket that opened is a different fact from a state that says listening - the recorded red was state=listening engine=deepgram, a test run authenticating on the operator's bill. The deadline is a timer that fires or does not.

what_it_proves: ui heard lands in MainWindow.OnHeard - the engine's own landing site - and nothing the decision layer can produce submits the box.
why_real_machinery: The operator's constraint is that speech can never send. Asserting it at the real landing site is the ONE LANDING SITE rule: a fake that fed a parallel path would prove nothing about the real one.

what_it_proves: ui answer -> AnswerAsk -> the daemon's answer -> the row closes, the overlay follows it down, and that question kind's real effect runs (a real git init with a first commit; a merge token actually granted).
why_real_machinery: One answer path over three question kinds, ending in effects that are real: a git repository that now exists on disk, and a token that is really held. It also carries the overlay-follows-the-row half, which is a live render.

what_it_proves: The overlay's choices exist in the live UIA tree as elements named ask:<value>.
why_real_machinery: The mechanical link between the pixels a person clicks and the value the verb takes. A dump can report a choice the visual tree never published; only the tree itself can refute that.

what_it_proves: Esc is view state only: the overlay goes down and the question row stays open and answerable.
why_real_machinery: A keypress at a live window plus a store row that must NOT have changed. The negative half is only meaningful against the real overlay that went down.

what_it_proves: A bare launch is the SHELL booted to zero - no dialog and no folder picker - it notices a workspace daemon that came up in another process with no operator action, and the workspace verb (the method a band click lands in) swaps the grid.
why_real_machinery: A second process coming up elsewhere and being noticed without any operator action is a poll across a process boundary. Boot-to-zero also asserts that no dialog and no filesystem picker appeared, which is an absence at a real window.

what_it_proves: A write from the window starts a SLEEPING workspace's daemon on demand - a real process comes into existence - on both the input-box path and the lane-tile path, and never answers daemon not running.
why_real_machinery: The exact path that shipped broken. A real daemon has to come into existence because of a click, which is an absence-then-presence claim about the process table, and the store must then show the action landed.

what_it_proves: A real MSBuild publish lays down one stamped versioned directory; daemon A hands off mid-turn to daemon B from that build and exits; the shim, the agent, the session and the in-flight turn survive with no loss and no double delivery; and the new daemon reports the new build and the commit MSBuild stamped into it.
why_real_machinery: The stamped commit only exists after MSBuild has really compiled an assembly, and the handoff is one live process replacing another while a turn is in flight. NOTE: this name also exists as m0:landed_exactly_once - a third cross-suite collision that W1.1 did not catch (see the commit message for this file).

what_it_proves: A candidate binary that cannot answer version --json is refused, and the system it was going to replace stays up.
why_real_machinery: The verification is a real child-process run of the candidate binary, and the survival claim is about the incumbent process still answering its pipe afterwards. Fourteen consecutive auto-publishes once repointed the shortcut at a binary whose daemon died on startup.

what_it_proves: A blocked swap arms itself and fires when the real blocker clears - and not before.
why_real_machinery: The not-before half is a real interval during which a real swap did not happen, which is an absence over wall clock and two processes.

what_it_proves: GcOldBuilds runs during a real reconcile and its retention vetoes the directory a live lane's deployed gate names.
why_real_machinery: Retention runs against real directories on disk while a real lane holds a gate registration pointing into one of them; a missing gate exe is a write gate that silently fails open.

what_it_proves: --all resolves targets from the REGISTRY: a live daemon belonging to another registry is neither named nor touched, and is still answering afterwards.
why_real_machinery: A foreign live daemon has to actually exist for the sparing to mean anything, and its survival is read off the OS - the survivor asserts the ORIGINAL pid never died, where a successor would also answer.

what_it_proves: Every target reports an outcome: a target that connects, reads and answers NOTHING is named and publish exits non-zero.
why_real_machinery: The fixture is a bare named-pipe server on a registered ctl pipe, which is what a silent no-op looks like at the wire. Silence is indistinguishable from success anywhere but here, and that is how the concierge ran a two-day-old build across many publishes.

what_it_proves: The concierge takes the swap over its own ctl pipe and the new process reports the new build.
why_real_machinery: The concierge is a real machine-global process; the evidence is that a DIFFERENT process is now answering, with a different build.

what_it_proves: A live shell window hot-swaps: it spawns a successor from a DIFFERENT binary path, hands off, and the successor serves the shell pipe as --shell.
why_real_machinery: The recorded incident is a successor that died at startup while the incumbent silently kept the old build. Only a real second binary path shows which process is answering; the sibling checks read an intention, or pass if no handoff was ever attempted.

what_it_proves: A build with no provenance refuses to watch, out loud, on a daemon started the way the operator starts one.
why_real_machinery: Provenance is compiled into the assembly by MSBuild, so the fixture is a real dev build image that knows no commit, on a daemon started with autostart cleared. This is CLAUDE.md section 3's every-suite-must-run-one-operator-path rule.

what_it_proves: An older store on disk is copied before it is migrated when a REAL daemon opens it, and the daemon comes up.
why_real_machinery: A Store migration that throws kills the daemon in its constructor, before the control pipe exists, so the daemon coming up at all is half the assertion and no in-process test can make it.

what_it_proves: A legacy store under the project root is physically relocated into workspace territory on first explicit resolve.
why_real_machinery: The files really leave one directory and arrive in another. The assertion is about the filesystem, not about a path a function computed.

what_it_proves: A typed --root NAMES a path and does not ADOPT one - asserted through status, i.e. through the RESOLUTION layer rather than through where, because Client resolves the workspace before any per-verb guard runs.
why_real_machinery: An absence-of-write claim over the concierge registry, and a DIFFERENT property from A7's no-summon: the folder-adoption incident is what proved they are two. A per-verb list could never have caught it, so it has to be asserted where resolution happens.

what_it_proves: The concierge is a real machine-global process on its own control pipe; it consults a tier agent child and acts on the answer; it stops when told.
why_real_machinery: Machine-global process lifetime plus a child agent round trip - neither is in-process - and the stop is a real exit observed on the OS.

what_it_proves: The concierge reviews an already-delivered sentence from behind and its verdict lands in the feed later.
why_real_machinery: The review runs behind a delivery that did not wait for it, so the ordering of two real actors across a process boundary is the claim.
